Discuss how old household shopping lists can help historians study daily consumption; mention a limitation without inventing citations. Aim for approximately 120–170 English tokens.

message.content:
Old household shopping lists can be valuable evidence for historians studying daily consumption because they record ordinary choices that are often missing from official documents. They can show what foods, cleaning goods, medicines, or small luxuries people bought, how often they shopped, and how budgets were managed. Changes in brands, quantities, or repeated items may reveal shifts in diet, technology, family size, health concerns, or social aspirations. Lists can also help connect domestic life to wider issues such as rationing, inflation, seasonal availability, and the spread of supermarkets.

A limitation is that shopping lists rarely explain context. They may not show what was actually purchased, who used the goods, whether items were shared, or why certain products were chosen. Surviving lists also tend to be accidental, so they may not represent all households equally.
